title.narrative: Strengthening Child-Centric Mental Health and Psychosocial support services in Chimanimani

description.narrative: CAFOD is currently implementing an integrated socio-economic resilience intervention (in Chimanimani, in partnership with the Oak Foundation and Caritas Mutare. Within the efforts to scale the impact of our work, CAFOD initiated a partnership with Refuge Zimbabwe, looking at jointly conceptualizing a model that will promote improved mental wellbeing and economic outcomes for vulnerable women. Research confirms that the high cost of living, high unemployment rates, and unstable economies provide a perpetual state of anxiety to both men and women of all age groups. The pilot aims to verify the links between improved mental wellbeing and economic choices. It is on these grounds that mental health and psychosocial support services are advanced as a complementary dimension to the existing and ongoing social and economic resilience building efforts in Chimanimani and particularly the desire to increase access to essential services (health, education, psycho-social support, justice) by survivors of GBV that Caritas Mutare is already working on.
